title: Bone Cancer
subtitle: Osteosarcoma (MAP), Ewing Sarcoma (VDC/IE), Chondrosarcoma, GCTB, and Chordoma
provenanceNote: Clinical algorithms extracted from NCCN Guidelines Version 1.2027 for Bone Cancer.
sourceNote: NCCN Guidelines Version 1.2027 - Bone Cancer (BONE-1, OSTEO-1, EW-1, CHON-1, GCTB-1, CHOR-1)

footnotes.fn_biopsy: Biopsy of suspected primary bone sarcoma MUST be performed at the treating orthopedic oncology referral center.
footnotes.fn_ewing_interval: Interval-compressed VDC/IE administered every 2 weeks is the category 1 standard of care for Ewing sarcoma.

nodes.name: Clinical Presentation
nodes.title: Primary Bone Tumors: Clinical Presentation & Initial Radiographic Finding
nodes.description: Patients presenting with persistent localized bone pain (frequently nocturnal), swelling, palpable osseous mass, or pathologic fracture.
bullets: Clinical presentation: deep, aching bone pain unrelieved by rest and worsening at night; soft-tissue swelling or palpable mass near metaphyseal region of long bones; pathologic fracture through an osteolytic lesion.

Initial radiographic suspicion: plain radiographs of involved extremity showing destructive bone lesion, cortical breakthrough, periosteal reaction (Codman triangle, 'sunburst' appearance, or 'onion-skin' layering).

Age Stratification: In patients <40 years, primary bone sarcomas (osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma) predominate; in patients >=40 years, metastatic carcinoma (breast, prostate, lung, kidney, thyroid) and multiple myeloma must be ruled out.

options.label: Suspected primary bone neoplasm - Proceed to multidisciplinary workup

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Bone Sarcomas: Biopsy, Staging, and Multidisciplinary Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Specialized biopsy at referral center, MRI of entire involved bone, chest CT, and systemic staging prior to definitive intervention.
bullets: Orthopedic Oncology Referral: Biopsy MUST be planned and performed at the treating tertiary sarcoma center by or in consultation with the orthopedic oncology team; poorly placed biopsy tracts can cause limb loss or preclude limb-sparing surgery.

Biopsy Principles: Longitudinal incision strictly parallel to limb axis; place track such that it will be entirely excised en bloc during definitive oncologic resection; meticulous hemostasis to prevent hematoma and compartment seeding.

Local Staging: Contrast-enhanced MRI of the entire involved bone including adjacent proximal and distal joints (essential to evaluate intramedullary extent, skip metastases, epiphysis/joint involvement, and neurovascular bundle proximity).
Metastatic Staging: Contrast-enhanced chest CT (or non-contrast thin-slice chest CT) to detect pulmonary metastases (the most common site of first recurrence).
Systemic Skeletal Staging: Whole-body FDG-PET/CT (preferred) or bone scintigraphy (99mTc-MDP bone scan) to detect occult skeletal metastases.
Laboratory Workup: Complete blood count, CMP, serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP), and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH; independent prognostic indicator).
Workup in patients >=40 years: Serum and urine protein electrophoresis (SPEP/UPEP/sFLC) to rule out myeloma; PSA in men; CT chest/abdomen/pelvis.
Fertility Counseling: Sperm banking or oocyte preservation discussion prior to alkylator/anthracycline-based chemotherapy.

nodes.name: Bone Sarcoma Subtype
nodes.title: Bone Sarcoma: Histopathologic & Molecular Classification
nodes.description: Histopathologic classification dictates whether chemotherapy, surgery alone, targeted therapies, or radiation are indicated.
bullets: Osteosarcoma: Malignant mesenchymal neoplasm producing malignant osteoid; high-grade conventional (intramedullary) is most common (~85%).
Ewing Sarcoma: Small round blue cell tumor harboring EWSR1 gene rearrangements (most commonly t(11;22) EWSR1::FLI1); CD99 strongly positive.
Chondrosarcoma: Malignant cartilaginous matrix-producing tumor (conventional grades 1-3, dedifferentiated, clear cell, mesenchymal).
Giant Cell Tumor of Bone (GCTB): Benign but locally destructive osteolytic neoplasm rich in osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells; driven by RANKL signaling.
Chordoma: Malignant tumor arising from embryonic notochord remnants in the axial skeleton (sacrum, skull base, mobile spine); brachyury positive.

nodes.name: Osteosarcoma Staging
nodes.title: Osteosarcoma: Localized vs Metastatic Disease Extent
nodes.description: Distinguish localized resectable disease from primary metastatic presentation.
bullets: Localized Disease: Confined to primary osseous site without distant metastases.
Metastatic Disease: Distant metastases at presentation (most commonly lungs ~80-85%, bones ~10-15%).

nodes.name: Localized Osteo MAP
nodes.title: Localized Osteosarcoma: Neoadjuvant MAP, Limb-Sparing Surgery & Adjuvant Chemotherapy
nodes.description: Category 1 multiagent perioperative chemotherapy and limb-salvage surgery.
bullets: Category 1 Preferred Frontline Regimen: MAP Regimen (High-Dose Methotrexate, Doxorubicin [Adriamycin], Cisplatin).
• High-Dose Methotrexate (12 g/m2 IV with leucovorin rescue and urine alkalinization), Cisplatin (100-120 mg/m2), and Doxorubicin (75 mg/m2) for 2 to 3 preoperative cycles (~10 weeks).
Definitive Surgical Resection (Limb Salvage vs Amputation):
• Wide surgical resection with negative margins (R0) and complete removal of biopsy tract; endoprosthetic reconstruction, allograft, or rotationplasty.
Pathologic Necrosis Assessment (Huvos Grading):
• Good histologic response (>=90% tumor necrosis): Resume and complete planned postoperative adjuvant MAP chemotherapy for a total of 29-32 weeks.
• Poor histologic response (<90% tumor necrosis): Complete remaining adjuvant MAP cycles; addition of ifosfamide and etoposide (MAPIE) has been utilized, though EURAMOS-1 showed equivalent survival.
Surveillance: Physical exam, local MRI/radiographs, and chest imaging (CT/x-ray) every 3 months for 2 years, every 6 months for years 3-5, then annually up to 10 years.

nodes.name: Metastatic Osteosarcoma
nodes.title: Metastatic Osteosarcoma: Systemic Chemotherapy & Metastasectomy
nodes.description: Intensive systemic therapy combined with aggressive surgical clearance of metastases.
bullets: First-Line Intensive Chemotherapy: MAP (Methotrexate, Doxorubicin, Cisplatin) or Cisplatin + Doxorubicin + Ifosfamide.

Surgical Metastasectomy (Potentially Curative): For patients with resectable pulmonary metastases achieving primary disease control, complete surgical resection of all lung metastases (thoracotomy/video-assisted thoracoscopy with wedge resections) yields long-term 5-year survival ~30-40%.
Subsequent Lines / Refractory Disease:

• Targeted Multikinase Inhibitors: Regorafenib (160 mg daily days 1-21 q28d) or Cabozantinib (60 mg daily) significantly prolong progression-free survival in relapsed/refractory osteosarcoma (REGOBONE / CABONE trials).
• Cytotoxic Salvage: Gemcitabine + Docetaxel, Ifosfamide + Etoposide, or High-Dose Ifosfamide.
• Bone-targeting radiopharmaceuticals: Radium-223 or Samarium-153 for widespread painful osteoblastic skeletal metastases.

nodes.name: Ewing Sarcoma VDC/IE
nodes.title: Ewing Sarcoma: Interval-Compressed VDC/IE & Local Control
nodes.description: Category 1 standard interval-compressed chemoimmunotherapy and local control.
bullets: Category 1 Preferred First-Line Strategy: Interval-Compressed VDC/IE (AEWS0031 trial):
• Vincristine (2 mg/m2), Doxorubicin (75 mg/m2), and Cyclophosphamide (1200 mg/m2 with mesna) alternating with Ifosfamide (1800 mg/m2/d x 5 with mesna) and Etoposide (100 mg/m2/d x 5).
• Administered every 14 days with mandatory G-CSF / filgrastim support; interval compression significantly improves event-free and overall survival compared to standard 3-week scheduling.
Neoadjuvant Phase: 9 to 12 weeks of VDC/IE prior to local control evaluation.
Local Control Modality (Week 12-14):
• Complete surgical resection with negative margins (preferred when functionally feasible).
• Definitive Radiation Therapy (50.4–55.8 Gy) for surgically unresectable lesions or positive surgical margins.
Consolidation Phase: Complete remaining cycles of interval-compressed VDC/IE (total of 14-17 cycles, ~28-30 weeks of therapy).
Relapsed/Refractory Options: Topotecan + Cyclophosphamide, Irinotecan + Temozolomide, High-dose Ifosfamide, Cabozantinib, or Lenvatinib.

nodes.name: Chondrosarcoma Subtype
nodes.title: Chondrosarcoma: Histologic Subtype & Dedifferentiation
nodes.description: Distinguish conventional chondrosarcoma (chemoresistant) from high-grade dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma.
bullets: Conventional Chondrosarcoma (Grades 1-3, Clear cell): Abundant cartilaginous matrix; resistant to conventional chemotherapy and radiation.
Dedifferentiated Chondrosarcoma: Biphasic tumor featuring low-grade cartilaginous component juxtaposed with high-grade non-cartilaginous sarcoma (e.g. osteosarcoma, MFH); extremely aggressive.

nodes.name: Conventional Chondro Tx
nodes.title: Conventional Chondrosarcoma: Surgical Resection & Targeted Agents
nodes.description: Wide oncologic resection is the primary curative modality.
bullets: Primary Curative Modality: Complete en bloc wide surgical excision with negative margins (R0 resection). Intralesional curettage with local adjuvant (phenol/cryotherapy) only acceptable for select low-grade intraosseous (ACT) appendicular lesions.
Chemotherapy & Radiation Resistance: Conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy has NO proven efficacy in conventional chondrosarcoma and is NOT routinely recommended.
Unresectable / Advanced / Metastatic Disease Management:
• Ivosidenib (500 mg PO daily): Targeted IDH1 inhibitor; highly effective in chondrosarcoma harboring susceptible IDH1 mutations (~50% of central chondrosarcomas).
• Multikinase Inhibitors: Pazopanib (800 mg daily) or Dasatinib.
• High-dose Particle Radiation (Proton or Carbon Ion RT) for anatomically unresectable skull base or axial lesions.

nodes.name: Dedifferentiated Chondro Tx
nodes.title: Dedifferentiated Chondrosarcoma: Osteosarcoma-Aligned Chemotherapy & Resection
nodes.description: High-intensity multiagent chemotherapy directed against the aggressive non-cartilaginous component.
bullets: Systemic Chemotherapy: Administer multiagent systemic chemotherapy directed at the high-grade sarcoma component per osteosarcoma protocols:
• Cisplatin + Doxorubicin, or MAP (Methotrexate, Doxorubicin, Cisplatin), or AIM (Doxorubicin, Ifosfamide, Mesna).
Surgical Resection: Radical en bloc resection of the primary tumor with wide margins; amputation may be necessary for large invasive lesions with vascular involvement.
Poor overall prognosis: Median survival remains guarded (<1-2 years); early multidisciplinary goals-of-care discussion and clinical trial consideration recommended.

nodes.name: GCTB Denosumab & Surgery
nodes.title: Giant Cell Tumor of Bone (GCTB): Denosumab & Joint-Preserving Surgery
nodes.description: RANKL targeted inhibition and intralesional curettage / resection.
bullets: Targeted RANKL Inhibition with Denosumab (Preferred Medical Therapy):
• Dose: 120 mg SC on days 1, 8, 15 of cycle 1, then 120 mg SC every 4 weeks.
• Indications: Unresectable tumors, sacral/spine lesions, or as preoperative downstaging therapy to reduce surgical morbidity and allow joint-preserving resection.

• Toxicity monitoring: Baseline dental examination prior to therapy to prevent osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ); daily calcium (500-1000 mg) and vitamin D (400-800 IU) supplementation to prevent hypocalcemia.
Surgical Treatment:

• Resectable lesions: Extensive intralesional curettage with high-speed burr drilling, supplemented with local chemical/thermal adjuvants (liquid nitrogen, phenol, or polymethylmethacrylate [PMMA] bone cement) and bone grafting.
• En bloc wide resection reserved for joint destruction or malignant transformation.
Malignant GCTB (Rare ~1-2%): Treat as conventional high-grade osteosarcoma.

nodes.name: Chordoma Resection & RT
nodes.title: Chordoma: En Bloc R0 Surgical Resection, Proton Beam RT & Targeted TKIs
nodes.description: Specialized skull base and sacropelvic oncology management.
bullets: Definitive Surgical Resection: En bloc wide surgical resection with negative margins (sacrectomy, mobile spine spondylectomy, or skull base endoscopic approach); positive margins carry high risk of local recurrence.
Advanced Radiation Therapy (Proton Beam / Carbon Ion Therapy):
• High doses (70–74 Gy RBE) required due to radioresistance; proton beam or carbon ion RT provides sharp dose fall-off sparing spinal cord and rectum.
• Indicated postoperatively for positive/close surgical margins or as definitive primary therapy for inoperable tumors.
Systemic Therapy for Unresectable / Metastatic Disease:
• Imatinib (400-800 mg daily; PDGFRB-directed) +/- Everolimus.
• Dasatinib, Sunitinib, or Lapatinib (for EGFR-expressing chordomas).
• Dedifferentiated chordomas: Doxorubicin + Ifosfamide (AIM regimen).
